text: This video demonstrates Driving Theory Practice, a revision tool for the Lithuanian driving theory test, made for the I B Computer Science internal assessment. Each success criterion is named on screen and then shown working. Test numbers refer to the test plan in criterion C.

Success criterion one is importing questions from a C S V file. When the app opens, the built-in bank of two hundred and twenty-one questions is loaded, and the number of valid questions is reported. This is test F 1.

Next, the button My own questions is used, and the file mixed ten is selected. It has seven valid rows and three invalid ones. The app loads seven questions and reports the three skipped rows, as test F 2 expects.

For reliability, an empty file is chosen. The app shows an error message, keeps the Start button disabled, and does not crash. A valid file, fixed thirty, can then be loaded straight away. This is test F 16.

The timer is switched on, which is success criterion six, and a session is started. It has thirty questions in random order, shuffled with the Fisher Yates algorithm, and the timer starts at zero. This is test F 3.
Each question shows its difficulty. A correct answer scores one point for an easy question, two for a medium one, and three for a hard one.
After a correct answer, the option turns green, the explanation appears, and the score rises straight away. This is success criterion four.
After a wrong answer, the chosen option turns red, the correct one turns green, and all options are locked, so the answer cannot be changed.
A whole session can also be completed with the keyboard. Keys A to D choose an answer, and Enter moves to the next question. The key hint stays visible on every question.
The remaining questions are answered quickly: the hard and medium ones correctly, and the easy ones wrongly, so that there are mistakes to practise later.

The results screen shows the total score and the percentage of the points available, the numbers of correct and incorrect answers, and the result for each difficulty. Because the timer was on, the time taken is shown to the second. These are tests F 9, F 10 and F 12.
Start New Session returns to the start screen without reloading the page. The new session is shuffled again, and the score and the timer start from zero. This is test F 13.
A session can also be ended early. After three answers, End session early saves the result, which covers only the questions that were answered. This is test F 23.

Success criterion nine is the history. Every session is saved on this device. The history screen shows statistics, a progress chart, the questions missed most often, and a review of the mistakes in each session.
Practise my mistakes starts a session made only of questions that were answered wrongly before. This is test F 20.

Success criterion ten is the user's own question bank. Two images are selected, and then a C S V file that also names a third picture, which is missing. The app loads three questions and reports the missing file by name.
In the quiz, the picture chosen by the user is shown with its question. This is test F 21.
The interface and the built-in bank can be switched to Lithuanian. The question numbers stay the same, so the history still matches. This is test F 22.
Finally, here are some examples of the testing.

The structural tests run inside the real application. Each major function is called with valid, extreme and invalid data, and all thirty-one tests pass. Test S 4 found a real defect with quotation marks in the C S V parser, which was then fixed.

In test F 24, every request that leaves the computer is blocked. The app still shows only the start screen, loads the bank and works. Before the fix, all four screens appeared at once without an internet connection.
The functional tests use only the interface: clicks, key presses and file uploads. All twenty-four functional tests pass. This completes the demonstration of every success criterion.
